Thanks for the ping, Marissa. Quick guidance from privacy/compliance here: 

- For an initial customer-facing roster, limit the columns to: Vendor name, Processing role (e.g., edge caching, monitoring, KMS), Country(ies) of processing, Cross-border transfer? (Yes/No), Transfer mechanism (if Yes: SCCs / adequacy / other). Avoid listing internal service endpoints or IP ranges.
- Redact any personnel contact info and internal hostnames.
- For high-risk subprocessors (KMS, HSM, key escrow, long-term logging), provide attestations and the date of the most recent audit, but send the underlying audit reports only after an NDA / secure transfer.
- We should proactively flag the observability vendor (LogNexus) and the transient caching partner (EdgeRipple) as "used for telemetry/caching" and mark whether they touch plaintext customer payloads. The current posture: EdgeRipple only touches encrypted caches (no decrypted customer PII) but LogNexus receives truncated telemetry metrics — include that language.

I'll attach a cleaned roster (redacted) and my suggested DPA Exhibit B redlines for Northern Trust. Upload the sensitive items to the secure Drive link below and do not include them in an unencrypted e-mail.

Attachments: subprocessor_roster_clean_v2.xlsx, dpa_exhibit_b_redlines.docx
Secure share: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cRedwoodSubprocV2
